Rosie vs Upfirst (2026)

These two charge differently, and that decides most cases. Rosie sells minutes. Upfirst sells calls and doesn't bill spam or calls under 15 seconds. Short calls favor Upfirst; long calls favor Rosie.

← All comparisons · Facts checked Oct 15, 2026 on vendor pages
RosieUpfirst
Entry plan$49/mo for 250 minutes$24.95/mo for 30 calls ($1.50 per extra call)
Higher tiers$149/mo for 1,000 minutes$59.95 (90 calls), $159.95 (300), $299 (600)
Annual discount2 months free20% off
Spam callsNot confirmed on vendor pageAI-blocked and not billed; calls under 15 seconds not billed
Calendar bookingBooks appointmentsGoogle, Outlook, Calendly, Acuity, Square, Clio
LanguagesNot confirmed on vendor page35+ languages
JobberVia ZapierVia Zapier
TrialNot confirmed14 days

"Not confirmed" means we couldn't find it on the vendor's own site. It may still exist, so ask them.

🧭 Which one should you pick?

  • Fewer than 30 real calls a month→ Upfirst Starter at $24.95.
  • Long calls (5+ minutes each)→ Rosie. You pay for minutes, and 250 minutes covers a lot of calls.
  • Lots of spam or robocalls→ Upfirst, since it doesn't bill blocked spam.
  • Several locations→ Upfirst adds extra agents at $9.95/mo each.
  • Callers in many languages→ Upfirst (35+ languages).

Questions people ask

Is Upfirst priced per call or per minute?Per call. Starter is 30 calls for $24.95/mo, then $1.50 per extra call.
Does Upfirst integrate natively with Jobber?No native integration. Upfirst connects through Zapier: Call Ended to Create Client.
Which has a longer free trial?Upfirst lists 14 days. We couldn't confirm a Rosie trial on its site.
